subject: Service guarantee tiering & monthly reciprocal remedy
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novaprospect.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novaprospect.com
Date: 2026-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Review: draft SLA — uptime & credits

Karthik,

Thanks for sending the draft SLA earlier today. Our procurement and platform teams reviewed and attached a short list of comments (Novaprospect-SLA-comments.pdf). High level items they want to surface before we move to signatures:

- Standard uptime: they are asking if we can commit to 99.95% for our production endpoints (this is a hard ask for their customer-facing systems).
- Monthly credit cap: procurement is concerned about an uncapped exposure and asked for a firm cap in dollars or percentage of the monthly invoice (they suggested 10% as a starting point).
- Latency carveouts: Novaprospect will run both low-latency interactive routing and large batched inference jobs. Their ops team requests tighter latency SLOs for real-time endpoints (p95 <= 300ms) and an explicit carveout for batch (p90 <= 1.2s) so those two can be governed separately.

Can you confirm what Redwood can offer as standard vs. add-on? Also: please share the credit calculation (monthly) and whether the cap can be a fixed percentage rather than an absolute dollar amount.

Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement — Novaprospect
elena.rossi@novaprospect.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachment: Novaprospect-SLA-comments.pdf (6 pages, annotated)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novaprospect.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Review: draft SLA — uptime & credits

Hi Elena — thanks for the notes and the annotated PDF. Quick summary of what we can propose so we can converge on a template: 

1) Tiered uptime: Redwood offers a default hosted SLA at 99.5% (no additional fee). For customers that need tighter guarantees (99.95%), we offer a "Production Premium" add-on (price uplift tied to committed spend). This gives you the stronger guarantee you asked for but as a billable option.

2) Latency split: We agree it's cleaner to split runtime classes. Proposal: label endpoints as RT (real-time) or BATCH. RT endpoints: p95 <= 300ms standard under Production Premium; BATCH endpoints: carveout with p90 <= 1.2s and separate credit triggers. We'll include explicit routing and tagging requirements in the appendix so there's no ambiguity.

3) Monthly credit cap: we can agree to a percentage-based cap. For negotiations, Redwood proposes a 15% monthly invoice cap for the first 3 months post-go-live (pilot/phased rollout), then re-evaluate. The credit formula would be pro-rata based on lost uptime and the affected endpoint population. We can also accept 12% as a compromise if it helps finalize.

I've attached a Redwood term sheet (redwood_sla_term_sheet_v1.pdf) that lays this out and a draft credit worksheet (redwood-credit-schedule.xlsx). If you can flag the items you want tightened we can move to DocuSign.

Thanks — looping Ben on commercial questions.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_sla_term_sheet_v1.pdf, redwood-credit-schedule.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novaprospect.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Review: draft SLA — uptime & credits (technical appendix & exception flow)

Karthik / Ben / Elena — quick technical addendum from product/ops: 

- Canary/rollout carveouts: for model rollouts that impact latency we recommend an exception clause that excludes "canary weeks" (first 14 days after a major model change) from credit calculations provided canary health checks are followed and we have a predefined rollback.
- Credit calculation: propose the formula be: monthly_credit = invoice_amount * min(credit_cap_pct, max(0, (target_uptime - observed_uptime)/target_uptime * weighting_factor)) where weighting_factor accounts for percentage of traffic on affected endpoints. I'll put a worked example in the appendix.
- Metric alignment: we need shared dashboards. Suggest a single Prometheus/Grafana read-only view or a CSV export cadence (daily) as evidence to avoid disputes.

Attached a latency appendix draft to show the RT vs BATCH tagging and measurement windows. If Novaprospect can accept the canary carveout and sampling window definitions, I think we can finalize the credit schedule and move to commercial.

Marissa Cole
Head of Product Ops — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
--
Attachment: latency-appendix-draft.md

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novaprospect.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novaprospect.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Review: draft SLA — uptime & credits

Karthik / Marissa — thanks for the detailed response and the appendix. Procurement has talked internally and they like the tiered approach: we will take the Production Premium option for our customer-facing endpoints but want the following modifications before signing: 

- Monthly credit cap: 12% of monthly invoice (final).
- Canary carveout: acceptable as long as the rollback and health-check criteria are documented in the appendix.
- Evidence: we prefer a daily CSV export plus a read-only dashboard link rather than Prometheus access.

If you can produce a final draft that reflects these three changes we can route to DocuSign. Please include the final credit worksheet and a single-page summary of RT vs BATCH tagging requirements. I will be the signer for Novaprospect (procurement).

Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement — Novaprospect
